articles.title: Kawhi Leonard sidelined again: Knee swelling forces Raptors star into rehab
articles.standfirst: Toronto fans received more bad news after defeat to the Minnesota Timberwolves
articles.summary: Toronto fans received more bad news after defeat to the Minnesota Timberwolves
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors are taking a cautious approach to Kawhi Leonard ’s latest knee problem, with the seven-time All-Star set to undergo treatment and rehabilitation for persistent swelling in his left knee. Imaging revealed no acute injury, but he will miss at least a week before being evaluated again next Tuesday and the setback follows Leonard ’s absence from Sunday’s 117-94 defeat against the Minnesota Timberwolves , when excess fluid in his knee forced him out shortly before tipoff.

Toronto had initially hoped to monitor the issue, but further medical assessments led the team to prioritize treatment over an immediate return as Leonard had started the 2026-27 campaign with 39 points across his first two appearances, although he shot just 32.4 percent from the field. His latest absence interrupts a season that began with expectations of a sustained run after he managed 65 games in 2025-26, his highest total since 2023-24 and the forward’s injury history adds significance to the decision. Leonard previously suffered a partially torn ACL in his right knee in 2021, missing the entire following season, before tearing his right meniscus in 2023. He has also dealt with recurring soreness and inflammation, although the current swelling affects his left knee.

Raptors slump to defeat without Leonard

Toronto struggled without him against Minnesota , falling to 2-1 despite 22 points from Ja’Kobe Walter and 20 from RJ Barrett as the home side shot 56 percent from the field and outrebounded the Raptors 49-34. Anthony Edwards led Minnesota with 26 points in only 27 minutes, while LaMelo Ball scored 15 in 16 minutes during his regular-season debut, the latter making four of five attempts from three-point range. Jaden McDaniels added 14 points, six rebounds and three blocks, while Rudy Gobert grabbed 13 rebounds. Minnesota shot 56 percent from the field and 48 percent from beyond the arc, also winning the rebounding battle 49-34 against Toronto . The Timberwolves established control defensively from the opening quarter, restricting the Raptors to nine made shots on 29 attempts whilst Leonard ’s side connected on just one of its first 10 three-point attempts. Allowing Minnesota to build momentum before stretching the margin to as many as 32 points, Toronto dropped to 2-1 despite having three players reach double figures, with the visitors unable to match the hosts’ efficiency. The Raptors are scheduled to host the Orlando Magic on Wednesday, but Leonard ’s rehabilitation timeline means the team must prepare to continue without him as his condition is reassessed.

articles.title: Josh Hart pretends to square up with Pistons assistant coach, scaring him during Knicks-Pistons scuffle
articles.standfirst: The Knicks guard pretended to square up with the Pistons assistant coach as players were being separated
articles.summary: The Knicks guard pretended to square up with the Pistons assistant coach as players were being separated
articles.body:
J osh Hart found a way to turn a tense moment at Madison Square Garden into something funny. During Tuesday’s game between the Knicks and Detroit, a scuffle broke out on the court. In an instant, Hart turned toward Pistons assistant coach Jarrett Jack and pretended to take a boxing stance . Jack seemed startled by the gesture and responded with a quick swat; Hart immediately lowered his hands and flashed a mischievous grin.

The moment caught people’s attention on social media because it happened in the middle of an intense game and seemed to come out of nowhere: Josh got the idea and acted on it in a matter of seconds.

Hart’s scare for Jarrett Jack came during a much-needed Knicks win

The altercation began as Karl-Anthony Towns and John Collins battled for a rebound. Collins hit Towns in the head and was assessed a Flagrant 1 foul. The play raised tensions on the court before Josh Hart’s unexpected, hilarious move.

The Knicks overcame a 13-point first-quarter deficit to beat Detroit 111-97, earning their first win of the season after an 0-3 start. The previously undefeated Pistons fell to 3-1. New York outscored Detroit 63-25 in the second and third quarters to take control of the game.

Karl-Anthony Towns led the Knicks with 27 points and 20 rebounds, while Jalen Brunson added 23 points and seven assists. Hart scored six points and finished with four rebounds, four assists and a game-high five steals. Paul Reed led Detroit with 22 points and nine rebounds.

But the moment from the night that may deserve the rewatch was the one involving the Knicks’ No. 3. His fake-out with Jack briefly shifted attention from the scuffle and helped defuse a tense moment that could have escalated into something much more serious on the court.

articles.title: The first NBA star to join OnlyFans: "He will post risqué content"
articles.standfirst: Lamar Odom, former Lakers, Heat, Maverick and Clipper, confirms to TMZ that he is making the leap to OnlyFans at 46 years old
articles.summary: Lamar Odom, former Lakers, Heat, Maverick and Clipper, confirms to TMZ that he is making the leap to OnlyFans at 46 years old
articles.body:
Lamar Odom is taking a turn in his career to become the first NBA star to join OnlyFans .

"When people hear "OnlyFans," they automatically think of just one thing; but I'm not here to tell them what they're going to see or what they're not," confirmed Lamar Odom, who played for Baskonia in the ACB League, to TMZ .

I have led a pretty intense life and, believe me, there are still a few surprises left. I have always been an open book, but there are chapters that people still have not seen

Lamar Odom (46 years old) acknowledges that "I have led a pretty intense life and, believe me, there are still a few surprises left. I have always been an open book, but there are chapters people have not seen yet."

Sources close to the former Clippers, Lakers, Heat, and Mavericks player consulted by TMZ confirmed that "Lamar Odom will post risqué content on his page, although, for now, nothing too extreme."

Lamar Odom and his dark story: sex, deaths, alcohol, drugs...

Lamar Odom spoke in February 2026 about his well-known drug addiction.

In a conversation with Tracy McGrady and Vince Carter on "The Cousins," he confirmed that he used drugs, specifically cocaine, especially during the summers

Lamar Odom, who nearly died in 2015 (he went into a coma) from a cocaine and stimulant overdose in a brothel , describes himself as "an addict" .

In 2015 I loved drugs, seriously. You're talking to a real addict. I used cocaine, I had no obligations," he confessed.

The two-time NBA champion noted that "he didn't use drugs while he was playing, but in the summers, he did. It would be crazy if he used cocaine and played at the same time."

"I had some incredible cocaine summers. I had it under control, but when you have the mind of a drunk, you think about how to beat the system. And that's what I did, cocaine parties," he admitted.

Amar Odom opened up about how his drug addiction began.

"The marijuana. A lot of people don't inherit addiction genetically. My father was a heroin addict. Marijuana doesn't get you high, like if you said: "Let me try cocaine." I started smoking at 14 or 15. It's also trauma. My mother died when I was 12... You're going to explode after losing your mother, my mother was my best friend... I remember that when I was 10 years old I told my mother I was going to the NBA and buy her a huge house, and by 12 she was gone," he said on "The Cousins".

articles.title: Where to watch Philadelphia 76ers vs Indiana Pacers? Today's LeBron James game time and prediction
articles.standfirst: Haliburton welcomes a Philadelphia team with Embiid and LeBron to Indianapolis
articles.summary: Haliburton welcomes a Philadelphia team with Embiid and LeBron to Indianapolis
articles.body:
G ainbridge Fieldhouse is preparing for one of the most attractive matchups at the start of the NBA season. The Indiana Pacers host the Philadelphia 76ers in an Eastern Conference clash that pits two playoff-ambitious projects against each other, but on very different paths in these opening weeks.

As Philadelphia settles in among the teams leading the East, Indiana looks to straighten out an uneven start in front of its home crowd. Here’s everything you need to know: tip-off time, where to watch it, and the keys to the game.

Where to watch the 76ers vs Pacers and start time

The matchup will be played this Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, a venue with a capacity of 17,274 fans. The start time of LeBron James' game with the 76ers will be:

As for the broadcast in the United States, the game will have national coverage on ESPN; in addition, fans will be able to stream it via YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo, DIRECTV, and Sling TV.

Standings overview for Philadelphia and Indiana

The picture in the Eastern Conference highlights contrasts. Philadelphia arrives in Indianapolis as the East's second seed , with a record of 3 wins and 1 loss (.750) that also puts them atop the Atlantic Division.

By virtue of points accumulated —440 scored to 428 allowed— it is a team that punishes on offense and has known how to take care of its opening commitments.

Indiana, meanwhile, sits in the middle of the standings. The Pacers are in ninth place in the East with 2 wins and 2 losses (.500), an identical record in the Central Division, where they are third behind the Detroit Pistons and Cleveland Cavaliers.

Their +6 differential (466 scored, 460 allowed) reflects close games and a fast pace: Indiana is one of the teams that generates the most possessions, a hallmark that could tip the balance if it manages to impose its tempo.

The players to watch in the 76ers vs Pacers

The box office is headed by the Pacers' franchise point guard, Tyrese Haliburton, the floor general who sets Indiana's frenetic pace through his playmaking . Around him, Pascal Siakam's interior presence and versatility provide the points and rebounds a team that lives to run needs.

The arrival of Croatian Ivica Zubac gives Indiana a strong defensive and rebounding anchor, while pieces like Aaron Nesmith, Andrew Nembhard and the experienced T.J. McConnell round out a deep and combative rotation.

Across from them, Philadelphia boasts one of the most eye-catching rosters in the league. Joel Embiid remains the dominant focal point in the post, with the ability to punish any interior defense.

Alongside him, guard Tyrese Maxey brings explosiveness and scoring from the perimeter , and the talent multiplies with the presence of two heavyweights like LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, who raise the Sixers' competitive ceiling. Veteran Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and young VJ Edgecombe round out a backcourt with shooting and energy.

What is the prediction for Pacers vs 76ers?

Philadelphia comes in with a better record, greater individual pedigree, and the confidence of sitting second in the East; without a doubt, the Sixers start as favorites. However, home-court advantage at Gainbridge Fieldhouse and the breakneck pace imposed by Haliburton could level the contest and turn it into a high-scoring duel decided in the final minutes.

The forecast points to a tight, offense-driven game, with a slight edge for Philadelphia if Embiid and Maxey maintain their level; but it wouldn’t be surprising if Indiana, at home and at full speed, pulls off the upset. A head-to-head matchup well worth not missing.

articles.title: Where to watch Lakers vs Clippers and What time is this Tuesday night's game starting?
articles.standfirst: Rematch battle for Los Angeles: the undefeated Lakers visit a desperate Clippers team at the Intuit Dome
articles.summary: Rematch battle for Los Angeles: the undefeated Lakers visit a desperate Clippers team at the Intuit Dome
articles.body:
The rivalry that has shared a city, a building for years, and now two different arenas is heating up once again. The Los Angeles Lakers , one of the few teams that still has not tasted defeat this season, cross the city to face the Los Angeles Clippers , who arrive with their backs against the wall after an uneven start. It is a Los Angeles showdown with a sense of urgency for the home team and a need for confirmation for the visitors.

Lakers vs Clippers: time and where to watch it live

The matchup between the two Los Angeles teams will be played on the night of Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at 10:30 p.m. Eastern Time (9:30 p.m. Central Time and 7:30 p.m. Pacific Time), at the Intuit Dome, the Clippers' home in Los Angeles, with a capacity of 18,300 spectators.

The local broadcast will be available through KTLA and the ClipperVision streaming service in the Clippers market, while the Lakers-side feed will air on Spectrum Sports Net and its Spectrum Sports Net + platform. In the rest of the United States, you can watch it with NBA League Pass.

The backdrop: one city, but two opposing trajectories

The photo of the standings tells the story forcefully. The Lakers come in with a 3-0 record, undefeated and atop the Pacific Division, while also moving into fourth place in the Western Conference.

Their point balance reflects a solid team on both sides of the court: 384 scored to 345 allowed, a +39 differential that matches that of several of the best in the West.

Across from them, the Clippers carry a 1-2 record, buried in ninth place in the West and on the second rung of the Pacific, two games behind their neighbors. It is not cause for panic—just three games played—but their +10 differential (339 points scored, 329 allowed) shows that they still have not found the consistency their roster promises.

Another stumble against their crosstown rival would intensify the pressure on a roster built to compete right away.

The Clippers' key players

The Clippers project has a veteran and ambitious face. The backcourt is led by Darius Garland and Bradley Beal, two offensive creators capable of carrying the load of the perimeter game.

On the front line, Brandon Ingram and Rui Hachimura stand out, along with the experienced Brook Lopez as an interior anchor and a threat from the three-point line. The rotation is rounded out by energy guys like Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus, and Kris Dunn, the latter a defensive specialist who can be key to containing opposing playmakers.

The challenge for the home team will be clear: to slow down the visitors' game plan and turn their offensive talent into sustained points throughout all four quarters, something their start to the season has not yet guaranteed.

The Lakers' unbeaten run rests on their star Luka Dončić, the engine that dictates the team's pace and shot volume. Alongside him, Austin Reaves provides secondary playmaking and scoring, while Collin Sexton and Quentin Grimes add dynamite from the perimeter with the second unit.

In the paint, the addition of Walker Kessler gives Los Angeles rim protection and rebounding, accompanied by veteran Kevon Looney and the versatile Jarred Vanderbilt, a defensive piece who can switch assignments across multiple positions.

The depth and balance of the roster largely explain that perfect start. If Dončić maintains the offensive rhythm and the interior defense keeps responding, the Lakers have the tools to keep adding wins.

What’s at stake in the Western Conference standings

For the Lakers, the game is an opportunity to extend their unbeaten run and strengthen their lead in the Pacific, establishing themselves among the teams in the West that still have not tasted defeat. A victory would leave them with a flawless 4-0 record and send a clear message in the divisional race.

For the Clippers, the margin is much narrower. A third loss would leave them at 1-3 and three games behind their neighbors in the division, an early deficit that, while recoverable, would start to weigh on them.

A win, on the other hand, would not only snap the Lakers' perfect streak: it would be the first major emotional boost of their season and a reminder that Intuit Dome can become a fortress.

Tonight's Lakers vs Clippers prediction

The difference in momentum is clear: the Lakers come in undefeated, with a better point differential and a star in top form, while the Clippers are still searching for their identity. Even so, crosstown matchups rarely follow the script, and the Intuit Dome home-court advantage should narrow the gap.

The edge goes to the Lakers, who should impose their consistency in a high-scoring game; but it wouldn’t be surprising if the Clippers take it down to the final minutes, driven by the urgency of avoiding a 1-3 hole. Slight advantage for the visitors in a matchup that promises plenty of points.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama gets bizarre request from NBA referee breaking the script
articles.standfirst: The Frenchman ended up helping the officials during the San Antonio Spurs' victory over the Sacramento Kings after the ball got stuck on top of the backboard.
articles.summary: The Frenchman ended up helping the officials during the San Antonio Spurs' victory over the Sacramento Kings after the ball got stuck on top of the backboard.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama is used to the San Antonio Spurs turning to him to solve situations on the court. This time, however, the request came from an unexpected place: one of the game’s referees.

The curious scene occurred during the third quarter of the game against the Sacramento Kings, when the ball ended up stuck on top of the backboard and play had to be stopped. Faced with the difficulty of retrieving it, one of the officials decided to turn directly to the 2.24-meter player.

articles.title: Ayesha Curry takes on a new role in Stephen Curry's life after rough season start with the Warriors
articles.standfirst: The Golden State star has praised wife Ayesha following an announcement that marks an important new chapter in her entertainment career
articles.summary: The Golden State star has praised wife Ayesha following an announcement that marks an important new chapter in her entertainment career
articles.body:
A difficult opening week for the Golden State Warriors has coincided with a significant career breakthrough for Ayesha Curry , giving husband Stephen Curry an opportunity to celebrate a personal milestone while navigating the challenges of another NBA season.

Golden State lost its opening three games before finally recording a victory against the Denver Nuggets on Monday, leaving the franchise with plenty to address as it attempts to establish momentum.

Away from basketball, however, Ayesha has been preparing for a major new chapter in her entertainment career, with the announcement that she will star in the upcoming romantic comedy Second Chance Holiday .

The movie represents her first leading role in a feature-length production, an achievement that immediately prompted a public message of support from her husband.

Curry shared the news through Instagram Stories on Tuesday, October 27, offering a personal acknowledgment of the work his wife has put into developing her career.

"My Leading Lady," Curry wrote alongside the announcement. "I get to see the work behind the scenes, and now the world gets to see you shine, and this is just the beginning..."

The message reflected a partnership that has increasingly extended beyond their family life into professional projects, particularly in film and theater.

Ayesha , who has built successful ventures in cooking, publishing and lifestyle businesses, has previously appeared in television productions and smaller film roles.

Her latest opportunity, however, places her at the center of a holiday romance alongside actor Matthew Daddario , marking a notable step forward in her acting career.

In Second Chance Holiday, Ayesha portrays Chelsey, a dating expert whose professional advice hasn't translated into success in her own relationships.

After repeatedly experiencing breakups during the holiday season, Chelsey becomes determined to change her romantic fortunes before an unexpected reunion with her high school sweetheart challenges her plans.

The film, directed by Maxwell McGuire , will premiere on The Roku Channel on November 5.

Ayesha Curry builds on Broadway and Hollywood success

The announcement follows a busy period for the couple, who have become increasingly involved in entertainment projects beyond Steph 's basketball career.

Earlier this year, they made their Broadway producing debut with The Lost Boys: A New Musical, which opened in April and subsequently earned 12 Tony Award nominations.

Both have also contributed to animated film projects, including GOAT, which premiered in February and featured Ayesha in a voice acting role.

Their involvement in theater and film reflects a growing interest in developing creative opportunities through Stephen's Unanimous Media production company.

Steph Curry looks for NBA turnaround

While Ayesha prepares for her movie premiere, Steph remains focused on helping Golden State recover from its disappointing beginning to the season.

The Warriors suffered defeats against the Los Angeles Lakers, Memphis Grizzlies and Phoenix Suns before securing a 134-114 victory in Denver.

That result offered some relief after an early stretch in which Golden State struggled to produce consistent performances.

Curry will now attempt to build on that improvement as the Warriors continue their schedule, but his wife's latest achievement has provided an additional reason for celebration.

After 15 years of marriage and four children together, the couple continues to support each other's professional ambitions, with Ayesha now preparing for one of the most prominent opportunities of her acting career.

articles.title: Internal Warfare? Stephen A. Smith reveals Knicks stars’ heavy resistance to James Dolan’s Trump invitation
articles.standfirst: Reports of possible resistance to a Donald Trump invitation have prompted questions about tension inside the defending NBA champions
articles.summary: Reports of possible resistance to a Donald Trump invitation have prompted questions about tension inside the defending NBA champions
articles.body:
Winning the NBA championship was supposed to bring a new era of celebration to Madison Square Garden, but Stephen A. Smith believes an unexpected disagreement could be threatening the atmosphere surrounding the New York Knicks .

Just four months after ending their 53-year championship drought, New York's players are reportedly reluctant to accept an invitation to visit President Donald Trump at the White House, despite owner James Dolan expressing enthusiasm for the occasion.

Smith raised the possibility of growing tension during Wednesday's edition of ESPN's First Take, suggesting that Dolan 's personal relationship with Trump could be complicating the situation.

"One of the things people have been talking about around New York City and Madison Square Garden is that the climate is different," Smith said.

"People have been a little bit stressed because the owner, James Dolan, has an attitude with players because they don't want to go to the White House."

Dolan 's connection with Trump has been publicly visible, particularly during the NBA Finals in June when the president attended Game 3 against the San Antonio Spurs at Madison Square Garden.

The Knicks owner subsequently indicated that the organization would accept an invitation to celebrate its championship at the White House.

Smith suggested that opposition from players could frustrate Dolan , whom he criticized sharply while discussing the rumors.

"I don't know whether this is true or not, but I'll believe anything when it comes to James Dolan because he is a walking embodiment of petulance," Smith said. "This man is as petty as they come."

The ESPN commentator went further, questioning how Dolan might respond if players ultimately rejected a visit.

"He's petty enough to have an attitude because he's tight with Trump and wants to go to the White House but some of the players, if not most of them, might not want to go," Smith added.

Knicks will make decision together

The uncertainty surrounding a potential visit was already apparent during September's training camp, when coach Mike Brown addressed the matter.

"No, it's still something that our guys, or the organization, is internally discussing and, you know, whatever we decide to do, we'll all do together," Brown explained.

NBA champions traditionally receive invitations to the White House, although no championship-winning team has made the visit during Trump 's presidencies.

The Knicks could potentially arrange a trip around their scheduled games against the Washington Wizards on December 18 or March 16.

Difficult championship defense begins

The speculation arrives during an uncomfortable opening to New York's title defense, with three consecutive defeats raising early questions about the team's performances.

However, the Knicks responded Tuesday by defeating the previously unbeaten Detroit Pistons 111-97, overcoming a 13-point first-quarter deficit.

New York outscored Detroit 63-25 across the middle two periods, showing the quality that carried the franchise to its historic championship.

While the victory provided some much-needed momentum, uncertainty surrounding a potential White House visit remains unresolved.

Smith 's comments have introduced the possibility of disagreement behind the scenes, but until players or ownership address the claims directly, the extent of any tension remains unclear.

articles.title: The Lakers unveil their plan to help Luka Doncic recover from his injury
articles.standfirst: The Lakers are taking no chances with Luka Doncic after the superstar was ruled out with back tightness.
articles.summary: The Lakers are taking no chances with Luka Doncic after the superstar was ruled out with back tightness.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers received bad news ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Clippers : Luka Doncic has been ruled out of Wednesday’s game due to back tightness.

The absence comes just one day after the Lakers suffered their first loss of the season, falling 136-129 to the Portland Trail Blazers in a game where Doncic once again led the offense with 41 points, nine assists, and five rebounds .

The Slovenian star will miss his first game of the 2026-27 season , although the franchise does not believe there is a serious long-term concern. According to Dan Woike of The Athletic , Los Angeles decided to be cautious with its superstar because of the team’s demanding upcoming schedule.

“A source says the Lakers are being cautious with Dončić and the back tightness as the team plays Game 2 in a stretch where the Lakers play five times in seven days,” the insider wrote. “No longterm worry about his health at this time.”

In addition to Doncic, the Lakers will also be without Cameron Carr (oblique injury), Adou Thiero (injury management), and Ziaire Williams (foot issue) against the Clippers.

Luka Doncic off to a blazing start with Lakers

Despite the loss to Portland, Doncic has enjoyed a spectacular start to the new season. Through four games, he leads the NBA in scoring average at 36 points per game , while also contributing 6.8 rebounds and 8.3 assists per contest .

The 27-year-old is coming off a historic performance against the Utah Jazz , where he recorded 52 points, 10 assists, and eight rebounds in a Lakers comeback victory.

His absence represents a major blow for a team that has built its new era around the Slovenian star following the departure of LeBron James , the extension of Austin Reaves , and the acquisition of Walker Kessler .

Lakers face a crucial stretch

The decision to rest Doncic also comes because of the challenging schedule ahead for JJ Redick’s team .

After facing the Clippers, the Lakers will take on the Golden State Warriors on October 30 and then face another back-to-back set against the Toronto Raptors and the Miami Heat on November 1 and 2 .

With five games in seven days, Los Angeles chose not to risk its franchise player and instead prioritize a full recovery before an important stretch of the season.

articles.title: Steph Curry threatens LeBron James' throne after tying another GOAT record
articles.standfirst: The 38-year-old produced another remarkable performance against Minnesota, leaving him one 40-point game away from history
articles.summary: The 38-year-old produced another remarkable performance against Minnesota, leaving him one 40-point game away from history
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors needed their greatest player to steady the team after a difficult opening to the season, and Steph Curry responded with the kind of performance that has defined his career.

Curry scored 44 points in Wednesday's 119-114 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves , delivering a reminder of his extraordinary scoring ability while reaching another milestone previously shared only by LeBron James .

The 38-year-old has now recorded 15 games with at least 40 points since his 35th birthday, matching James for the most in NBA history.

It was another demonstration of Curry 's remarkable longevity, particularly after injuries limited his availability last season and forced Golden State to manage his playing time carefully.

Although the Warriors had built a commanding 24-point advantage during the second half, Minnesota threatened an unlikely comeback, leaving Curry 's contributions essential to securing the victory.

Curry 's latest scoring exhibition didn't begin particularly smoothly, with the veteran making only two of his first eight field-goal attempts.

However, his fortunes changed dramatically during the second quarter, when he produced a devastating burst of outside shooting that transformed Golden State's position.

Curry scored 19 points during the period, helping the Warriors establish a 64-48 halftime advantage.

His scoring eventually reached 44 points, accompanied by eight rebounds and six assists, but one statistic illustrated how effectively he adapted to Minnesota's defensive pressure.

Curry converted all 16 of his free throws, marking the first time in his career he had attempted that many without missing.

"They were pressuring pretty much all the way out to half court, so you're gonna have those driving lanes," Curry explained afterward.

"Thankfully it helped us in a couple lulls that we had, getting to the line, getting easy buckets, which we needed all of them."

Steve Kerr explains why Curry remains so dangerous

Warriors coach Steve Kerr has watched Curry produce countless scoring explosions, yet his ability to change a game within minutes remains central to Golden State's success.

"I just see him doing what Steph Curry does," Kerr said after Wednesday's victory. "I've been watching him for so long that it never surprises me when he gets hot. What makes him special is it can happen at any time."

The Warriors also benefited from an impressive performance by rookie Yaxel Lendeborg , who contributed 26 points and nine rebounds.

Minnesota, meanwhile, played without Anthony Edwards , who faces an extended absence following knee surgery.

Despite that advantage, Golden State struggled to protect its substantial lead before securing a second consecutive victory.

LeBron James record comes into view

Curry 's latest achievement carries additional significance because Golden State continues to monitor his workload after injuries disrupted the previous campaign.

The veteran has been operating under a 32-minute restriction, designed to protect his health while allowing him to regain his rhythm.

He played almost his full allowance against Minnesota, showing confidence in his physical condition despite the demands of his 18th NBA season.

"I honestly didn't know until after the game, which was nice that we were just kind of in the moment, playing," Curry said when discussing his minutes. "So it's nice to keep building and feel good coming out of it."

Golden State now returns home to face the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday, with Curry potentially sharing the court with James .

Another 40-point performance would move Curry clear of his longtime rival and establish a new NBA record for scoring performances after age 35.

However, the immediate significance of Wednesday's display was equally important: after three opening defeats, Golden State has rediscovered some momentum, with its greatest player leading the recovery.

articles.title: In 2010, Michael Jordan made a risky investment that turned into a $3 billion deal 13 years later
articles.standfirst: The former player paid about $275 million for control of the Charlotte Hornets, and in 2023 he sold his majority stake in a deal that valued the franchise at $3 billion.
articles.summary: The former player paid about $275 million for control of the Charlotte Hornets, and in 2023 he sold his majority stake in a deal that valued the franchise at $3 billion.
articles.body:
Michael Jordan paid approximately $275 million in 2010 to become the majority owner of the then-Charlotte Bobcats. Thirteen years later, the sale of his controlling stake was completed in a deal that valued the franchise at about $3 billion.

The NBA approved Jordan's acquisition in March 2010, although the former player had already been part of the ownership group for four years. With that transaction, he became the first former NBA player to assume majority control of a franchise.

From $275 million to a $3 billion valuation

In August 2023, the sale of Jordan's majority stake to a group led by Gabe Plotkin and Rick Schnall was completed. Plotkin had already been a minority shareholder of Charlotte since 2019, while Schnall arrived after having been part of the ownership group of the Atlanta Hawks. Jordan, for his part, decided to retain a minority stake in the Hornets.

The difference between the 275 million paid in 2010 and the 3 billion valuation in 2023 shows how much the value of the franchise increased during those 13 years.

During his time leading the organization, one of the team's most important identity changes also took place. The franchise left behind the Charlotte Bobcats name and brought back the Charlotte Hornets name for the 2014-15 season, a change driven during Jordan's tenure.

The on-court results, however, were far from matching the economic growth. Charlotte compiled a record of 423 wins and 600 losses during Jordan's 13 seasons as majority owner, made the playoffs three times, and failed to win a postseason series.

The contrast was clear: while the team struggled to establish itself as a contender in the Eastern Conference, its valuation increased more than tenfold compared with the amount Jordan paid in 2010. The 2023 deal thus brought his tenure as majority owner to a close after more than a decade at the helm of the franchise.

Jordan did not completely sever ties with Charlotte. After the sale, he continued as a minority shareholder and Alternate Governor of the Hornets, according to the franchise's official information, maintaining a relationship with the team that began years before assuming control in 2010.

articles.summary: Boogie Cousins believes the Warriors must either build around their franchise icon or trade him to a team with genuine championship ambitions
articles.body:

articles.title: Hypocrisy or just basketball? The NBA world tears into Luka Doncic for complaining about Damian Lillard’s tricks
articles.standfirst: Fans question Luka's reaction after Damian Lillard uses a familiar trick against the Lakers star
articles.summary: Fans question Luka's reaction after Damian Lillard uses a familiar trick against the Lakers star
articles.body:
Luka Doncic found himself on the receiving end of a familiar basketball tactic when the Los Angeles Lakers faced the Portland Trail Blazers, and fans haven't been shy about pointing out the irony.

Despite Doncic's impressive individual performance, Portland secured a 136-129 victory on October 27.

However, an intriguing second-quarter exchange between the Lakers superstar and Damian Lillard became one of the game's biggest talking points.

With 2:44 remaining before halftime, Doncic drew a shooting foul while Portland held a 61-59 advantage. The Slovenian guard raised his arms and appeared amused by the situation, with Lillard and Donovan Clingan nearby.

He subsequently converted all three free throws, giving Los Angeles a brief lead.

The moment took an interesting turn less than a minute later. At the 1:34 mark, Lillard appeared to employ a similar foul-drawing move, earning three free throws after Doncic was called for the shooting foul.

During the sequence, Doncic appeared to take contact around his jaw and remained on the floor briefly. His teammates gathered around him as he eventually stood up, continuing to work his jaw. One broadcaster even joked that the Lakers star might need a dentist.

Lillard missed his first attempt but converted the remaining two, putting Portland ahead 65-64.

Doncic's reaction sparks questions about a double standard

The exchange reignited discussions about Doncic's reputation for drawing fouls and using exaggerated reactions to attract officials' attention.

The Lakers guard has frequently frustrated opposing supporters with his ability to manufacture contact and get defenders into difficult situations. Yet when an opponent appears to use comparable tactics, the conversation becomes considerably more complicated.

“Luka foul baits and laughs, then Dame does the same thing to him, and he cries,” wrote one fan.

“This is why Yaxel called him out on game 1. Luka nonstop crying,” wrote another.

Meanwhile, there's encouraging news for Los Angeles ahead of Friday's NBA Cup meeting with the Golden State Warriors. Doncic isn't listed on the Lakers' injury report after missing Wednesday's 103-87 victory over the Clippers because of back tightness.

He's averaging 36.0 points, 6.8 rebounds and 8.3 assists through four appearances, shooting 48.4% from the field.

With Doncic expected back, the Lakers will have their leading offensive weapon available. Adou Thiero remains sidelined with a left knee injury, while Ziaire Williams is questionable.

After the Portland talking point, all eyes will be on Doncic as he looks to deliver another statement performance.

articles.title: Shaq exposes Charles Barkley’s championship slip-up in hilarious ‘Inside the NBA’ exchange
articles.standfirst: The exchange highlighted an important part of Kyrie Irving's responsibilities with the Mavericks
articles.summary: The exchange highlighted an important part of Kyrie Irving's responsibilities with the Mavericks
articles.body:
C harles Barkley has never been shy about giving NBA players a hard time, but when it comes to championship rings, the Hall of Famer remains an easy target for his longtime Inside the NBA colleague Shaquille O’Neal.

That dynamic was on full display Wednesday night after the Dallas Mavericks defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder, when Kyrie Irving joined the TNT Sports crew for a conversation about leadership, experience and mentoring younger players. What began as a thoughtful discussion about Irving's role with Dallas quickly turned into another opportunity for Shaq to remind Barkley of the one major achievement missing from his legendary basketball career: an NBA championship.

The awkward moment happened as Barkley asked Irving how he approaches mentoring younger teammates who might not fully appreciate the experiences of an established NBA veteran. "How do you balance, 'I need to teach these young guys, I've been through it?'" Barkley asked.

The 63-year-old analyst then explained that younger players sometimes struggle to understand the perspective of older athletes because they have never experienced the same challenges. "A lot of times, it's like when we're talking to our kids, they think we're born old," Barkley said.

He continued by listing the accomplishments and experiences that allow veteran players to offer advice to younger teammates. "I've been a young great player; I've won the world championship; I've been an All-Star multiple times. How do you balance that, like, 'Guys? I've been through the wars, just listen to me?'"

There was just one problem with that statement

As soon as Barkley mentioned winning a world championship, Shaq interrupted him with a perfectly timed question. "You've won what?" The remark immediately drew laughter from Irving, who understood exactly where O'Neal was going with the joke.

Barkley , of course, never won an NBA championship during his 16-season career. Despite becoming one of the greatest power forwards in league history, winning the 1993 NBA MVP award and earning 11 All-Star selections, a championship ring eluded him.

O'Neal, meanwhile, knows a thing or two about winning titles. The former Los Angeles Lakers and Miami Heat center captured four NBA championships, giving him plenty of ammunition whenever Barkley's postseason résumé becomes part of the conversation. But the best part of the exchange came later in the broadcast, when Barkley appeared confused about why his colleague had interrupted him.

"What did I say?" Barkley asked. Shaq did not miss the opportunity to explain. "I just wanted him to stop lying," O'Neal responded before imitating Barkley's statement: "I won a world championship."

The joke was particularly effective

Barkley had technically said those words, but he was not actually talking about his own career. He was speaking from Irving's perspective, essentially role-playing as the Mavericks guard to illustrate how a veteran might explain his accomplishments to younger teammates.

Irving is, after all, an NBA champion . He won the 2016 title with the Cleveland Cavaliers, delivering one of the most memorable shots in NBA Finals history when he buried a three-pointer over Stephen Curry in Game 7 against the Golden State Warriors. Barkley's wording created the perfect opening for Shaq, who was more than happy to take advantage of it.

Beyond the comedy, the exchange highlighted an important part of Irving's responsibilities with the Mavericks. At 34, the veteran guard is among the experienced leaders on a Dallas roster whose future revolves around young talent, particularly rising superstar Cooper Flagg.

Irving's championship experience and years competing at the highest level give him a valuable perspective as the Mavericks look to develop their younger players and build a team capable of contending in the Western Conference.

A title that never came for Barkley

The guard has experienced virtually every stage of an NBA career, from becoming a No. 1 overall draft pick in 2011 to winning a championship alongside LeBron James in Cleveland and later taking on leadership responsibilities with other franchises.

That background was precisely what Barkley wanted to discuss. Instead, Shaq turned the conversation into another reminder that the former Phoenix Suns and Philadelphia 76ers star never managed to capture the NBA title that defined so much of his career.

Barkley reached the NBA Finals once, in 1993, when his Phoenix Suns faced Michael Jordan and the Chicago Bulls. Despite winning Game 3 in triple overtime, Phoenix u ltimately lost the series in six games. It remains one of the biggest missing pieces in Barkley's otherwise extraordinary basketball résumé.

The exchange also comes during what could be the final stretch of one of sports television's most entertaining partnerships. Barkley has indicated that he plans to retire alongside longtime Inside the NBA host Ernie Johnson after the current season, potentially bringing an end to years of memorable debates, arguments and comedy alongside O'Neal and Kenny Smith.

articles.title: Dwyane Wade was blowing millions and nearly lost everything until a wake-up call from his own body changed everything
articles.standfirst: The NBA legend understood that his financial future could not depend entirely on remaining healthy enough to play basketball
articles.summary: The NBA legend understood that his financial future could not depend entirely on remaining healthy enough to play basketball
articles.body:
Making millions of dollars in professional sports is a dream for countless athletes, but earning a fortune and knowing how to preserve it are two very different challenges. Dwyane Wade learned that lesson after years of enjoying the rewards of NBA superstardom, when a frightening injury forced him to reconsider how quickly his wealth could disappear.

The three-time NBA champion spent much of his early professional career buying the things he had always wanted. Luxury cars, expensive homes and an increasingly extravagant lifestyle became part of his reality after going from a difficult childhood to becoming one of basketball's highest-profile stars.

But an unexpected wake-up call changed his relationship with money. Wade realized that his playing career, and the enormous income that came with it, could end much sooner than expected. Suddenly, the possibility of losing his ability to earn millions made his spending habits look considerably different.

During a recent appearance on the Let It Fly Podcast, hosted by Jared Dillinger, Sol Mercado and Suzy Gamboa, the former Miami Heat superstar opened up about the financial mistakes he made during his playing days and how an injury ultimately pushed him toward financial discipline.

"My mindset started to change. I was like, 'All right, we're not just about to just spend money no more. We're actually going to like, find a money manager,'" Dwyane explained. It was a realization that went beyond purchasing fewer luxury items. Wade understood that his financial future could not depend entirely on remaining healthy enough to play basketball.

From NBA superstardom to an expensive lifestyle

Wade's financial transformation came after he had established himself as one of the NBA's premier players. Selected fifth overall by the Miami Heat in the 2003 NBA Draft , he quickly became a franchise cornerstone. His breakthrough came in 2006, when he led Miami to its first NBA championship, earning Finals MVP honors after a remarkable performance against the Dallas Mavericks.

His success translated into enormous financial rewards. Following the championship, Wade signed a three-year, $63 million contract, further expanding his wealth and purchasing power. But his spending habits were also growing.

One of his biggest weaknesses was luxury automobiles. Wade enjoyed collecting expensive vehicles, even when he rarely had time to drive them. Eventually, his financial adviser, Ginger , confronted him about the costs associated with maintaining his collection and encouraged him to make some difficult decisions.

Wade recalled one particularly expensive example: a Maybach that was costing him approximately $6,000 per month despite barely being used. "My financial advisor, Ginger , came in and said, 'Okay, so that Maybach, the one that costs you $6,000 a month, you don't drive it. How about we get rid of that?'" Wade remembered.

His injury made him understand how vulnerable his income could be

The conversation eventually led Wade to sell approximately 16 vehicles. For someone accustomed to buying whatever caught his attention, giving up that collection represented a significant change in perspective. He began recognizing that owning expensive possessions was not necessarily the same as building lasting wealth.

His injury had already made him understand how vulnerable his income could be. His financial adviser helped him turn that realization into action. Wade wasn't the only NBA superstar who struggled with money. Wade's experience reflects a broader challenge in professional sports: young athletes can suddenly receive enormous contracts before developing the financial knowledge needed to manage them.

Shaquille O'Neal, another NBA legend, has openly discussed his own early financial mistakes. The former Lakers and Heat center once recalled spending his first $1 million paycheck almost immediately. Among his purchases were a $150,000 Mercedes-Benz and additional luxury vehicles for his parents, along with jewelry, clothing and other expensive items.

The biggest problem was that O'Neal had not properly accounted for taxes and other deductions. "I had no idea what FICA, and income, state tax, sales tax were," O'Neal admitted when discussing his financial education.

Wade now wants to help the next generation avoid those mistakes

Wade's experience has influenced what he wants to accomplish away from the basketball court. Rather than simply discussing the mistakes he made, the former NBA star is now involved in efforts to improve financial education for professional athletes and those preparing to enter the industry.

As chairman of JPMorgan Chase's Athlete Council, Wade is working alongside prominent sports figures, including Tom Brady, Sue Bird and A'ja Wilson, to help athletes make more informed financial decisions. The initiative focuses on providing financial guidance throughout an athlete's career, from college opportunities and name, image and likeness (NIL) agreements to professional contracts, endorsements and retirement planning.

The objective is to help athletes understand how to manage their money before they encounter the financial difficulties that have affected some of their predecessors. It is particularly relevant as college sports continue to evolve and athletes gain access to new revenue opportunities through NIL agreements.
